channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Khatlon Region Produces Over Half of Tajikistan's Agricultural Output
item.description: Tajikistan's agricultural production reached 35.7 billion somoni, an 8.2% increase year-on-year. The Khatlon region contributed 53.3% of the total output. Significant gains were reported in crop yields, including grains, potatoes, vegetables, and fruits, alongside livestock production.

item.title: UN-Habitat: 100 Families in Herat Gain Access to Safe Drinking Water
item.description: UN-Habitat announced that 100 families in Herat's Zinda Jan district now have access to safe drinking water, thanks to support from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). The water is connected directly to homes and available 24/7, improving health and living conditions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sets Campaign Spending Limits for Local Council Candidates
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has set spending limits for candidates running for local council seats. The limits vary based on the level of the council (regional, city, or district) and cover expenses for media, public events, campaign materials, and transportation. Candidate nomination closes October 27.

item.title: Stronger Afghani Fails to Offset High Food and Fuel Costs in Afghanistan, WFP Reports
item.description: Despite a stronger Afghani currency, the World Food Program reports that prices for staple foods, fuel, and agricultural inputs remain significantly higher than last year in Afghanistan. Disruptions to regional trade routes and slower imports are exacerbating these costs. Rice prices have seen substantial year-over-year increases, with Sholae rice up 32% and Palawi rice up 18%.

item.title: UN: Phase Two of Economic Recovery Begins in Five Afghan Provinces
item.description: The United Nations has announced the commencement of the second phase of economic recovery initiatives across five provinces in Afghanistan. This phase aims to further stabilize and develop the local economies, building upon the progress made in the initial stage. Specific details regarding the projects and targeted sectors were not immediately available.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Grants First Islamic Banking License to Open Bank
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has issued the first license for Islamic financial services to Open Bank JSC. The license, effective October 23, 2026, allows the bank to offer services compliant with Islamic finance principles. The Central Bank advises citizens to verify commercial banks' licenses on the official website before using their services.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Tatarstan Establish Consortium for Snow Leopard Study
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Tatarstan have signed an agreement to create a consortium focused on studying and restoring snow leopard populations. The collaboration will involve research centers in both regions, with a focus on genetic diversity, population monitoring, and breeding techniques. The initiative also aims to establish biobanks and facilitate specialist training.

item.title: Direct Flight Launched Between Astana and Kulja, China
item.description: Kazakhstan's low-cost carrier FlyArystan has launched a direct flight route connecting Astana with Kulja (Yining), China. The inaugural flight departed from Astana's Nursultan Nazarbayev International Airport. Flights will operate three times a week, with ticket prices starting from 34,500 tenge. Kulja serves as a gateway to the Ili River Valley.

item.title: Uzbekistan Issues First Islamic Banking License to Open Bank
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has issued the first license for Islamic banking operations to Open Bank Joint Stock Company. This marks a significant development in the country's financial sector, allowing for the introduction of Sharia-compliant financial services. Further details are expected regarding the scope and operations of the licensed entity.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev thanks international counterparts for Republic Day greetings
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev expressed gratitude to heads of state and government, as well as leaders of international organizations, for their Republic Day greetings. He stated that the nation received their well wishes with appreciation. Numerous leaders from countries including the US, Russia, China, and Turkey had sent congratulatory messages on the national holiday.

item.title: Conversion of future Kokshetau thermal power plant from coal to gas ruled out
item.description: The company 'Kokshetau Thermal Power Plant' has excluded the possibility of converting its future plant in Kokshetau from coal to gas. The plant's commissioning is postponed to the third quarter of 2028. While gas is considered an alternative fuel, its stable supply is currently unfeasible due to the lack of gasification in the region.

item.title: New Irrigation Well Nears Completion in Bishkek's Park
item.description: Bishkek's municipal enterprise 'Bishkekzelenstroy' is completing a new irrigation well in Park 'Emeen' and the 'Governmental' square. The 120-meter deep well will produce 120 cubic meters of water per hour, sufficient for irrigating up to 15 hectares. Two more wells are planned by year-end to enhance the city's green infrastructure.

item.title: 19 years later, brother of murdered journalist Alisher Saipov seeks truth
item.description: Nineteen years after the murder of Osh-based journalist Alisher Saipov, his family still does not know who was responsible. His brother, journalist Shokhrukh Saipov, shared memories and reiterated the family's ongoing pursuit of justice for the killing, which involved three gunshot wounds.

item.title: Tajikistan delegation participates in World Investment Forum in Qatar
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade attended the 9th World Investment Forum in Doha, Qatar, under the theme 'Invest in the Future'. The forum, running from October 25-27, 2026, discusses climate change adaptation, green investments, food security, and green energy.

item.title: UN Launches Second Phase of Economic Recovery Program in Five Afghan Provinces
item.description: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) announced the second phase of its REVIVE II program to support economic recovery in five Afghan provinces. The initiative will focus on strengthening livelihoods, rebuilding infrastructure, revitalizing the economy, and improving community resilience in Kabul, Paktia, Ghazni, Nangarhar, and Kunar.

item.title: Over 4,000 Mortgage Apartments Under Construction in Batken, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The State Mortgage Company (SMK) is constructing over 4,000 mortgage apartments in Batken, Kyrgyzstan, across three multi-story buildings. The project includes wastewater treatment facilities, a 12,000 cubic meter water reservoir, four wells, and a 35-megawatt substation, with a total cost of 228 million soms. Approximately 3,500 people are on the waiting list for housing.

item.title: Tajikistan's State Budget Revenue Increases by Nearly 15% in Nine Months
item.description: Tajikistan's state budget revenue has seen a significant increase of nearly 15% over the first nine months of the year, reaching 57.1 billion somoni. The article questions the sources of this substantial revenue growth, indicating a need for further explanation on how this increase was achieved.

item.title: Kyrgyz National Bank Adjusts Minimum Credit Risk Management Requirements
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has amended regulations for credit risk management in financial institutions. New rules include a mandatory waiting period for online loans, with specific times based on loan amount. These changes take effect from December 1, 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks Among Top Three EAEU Countries in Industrial Growth
item.description: Kazakhstan has secured a position among the top three leaders in the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) for industrial growth. This ranking highlights the country's recent performance in its industrial sector within the regional economic bloc.

item.title: Haqqani Allies Replace Police Academy Instructors in Afghanistan
item.description: Close associates of Taliban Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani have replaced 15 instructors at Afghanistan's National Police Academy. Sources reported the dismissed instructors, some with over 30 years of experience, were removed without explanation. New appointees previously served in Taliban ranks.

item.title: Kazakh President Thanks Foreign Leaders for Republic Day Congratulations
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev expressed gratitude to foreign leaders for their congratulations on Republic Day. He thanked heads of state, government, and international organizations for their warm wishes, noting that the goodwill towards Kazakhstan is appreciated by its people. Several leaders, including those from Russia, China, the US, and Turkey, sent congratulatory messages.

item.title: Former Kyrgyz Financial Police Chief Passes State Language Test for Presidential Run
item.description: SyyMyk Japykeev, former head of Kyrgyzstan's financial police and a presidential hopeful, has successfully passed the state language proficiency test. He previously failed the written portion in October but retook and passed the exam on October 21. Presidential elections are scheduled for January 27.

item.title: Woman Sentenced to 13 Years for Stabbing Husband's Wife and Daughter
item.description: A court in Shirin, Sirdaryo region, sentenced a 29-year-old woman to 13 years and 4 months for fatally stabbing her husband's legal wife and one daughter, and injuring another. The incident occurred in April following disputes over children. The court applied articles related to attempted murder and murder under aggravating circumstances.

item.title: Kazakhstan Inmates Injure Themselves in Protest Over Prison Conditions
item.description: Five inmates at an Atyrau detention center in western Kazakhstan inflicted self-harm on October 23 to protest living conditions. They demanded the transfer of individuals from the quarantine block. Reports indicate dissatisfaction with sanitation, sewage, food quality, and restrictions on permitted deliveries. An investigation has been launched.

item.title: Employer Conceals Workplace Injury, Leaving Single Mother Amputee Without Adequate Support
item.description: A single mother raising three children lost a leg after a tower crane collapsed at an Astana construction site. Her employer allegedly promised compensation equivalent to three months' salary but failed to provide sufficient support. The woman, who has a mortgage, stated she cannot return to her previous job. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Clarifies Personal Data Storage Requirements for Digital Platforms
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development has clarified that personal data of citizens must be stored in databases located within the country, in compliance with local legislation. This requirement applies to foreign digital platforms operating in Kazakhstan. While using foreign server infrastructure is permitted under certain conditions, data must be protected. The ministry is continuously improving legislation on personal information security and digital infrastructure resilience.

item.title: Astana Police Launch Criminal Case Over Alleged Child Molestation in Residential Complex
item.description: Astana police have opened a criminal case against a man suspected of molesting a young girl in a residential complex. The incident was reported by a resident who shared surveillance footage online. The police are investigating under the article of "sexual assault of a minor." The security measures within the residential complex are also being questioned.

item.title: New Autonomous Trolleybuses to Launch in Uzbekistan's Khorezm Region on October 27
item.description: New autonomous trolleybuses, manufactured by China's Yutong, will commence service on the Urgench-Khiva route starting October 27. This follows the opening of a new administrative building and depot for the "Khorezm Trolleybus Park" state enterprise in Urgench. Drivers have completed specialized training. Khorezm is the only region in Uzbekistan with a preserved trolleybus system.

item.title: Driver Dies After Car Collides with Bus in Kostanay
item.description: A driver has died following a collision between a Volkswagen Passat and a bus in Kostanay. Police reported that the car driver disregarded a stop signal and ran a red light, crashing into the bus. The driver of the car sustained fatal injuries, while a passenger was hospitalized. Two bus passengers received medical attention at the scene.

item.title: Serbian Progressive Party Admits Defeat in Parliamentary Elections
item.description: Aleksandar Vučić, leader of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), has conceded defeat in the parliamentary elections held on Sunday. Preliminary results show the SNS securing 105 seats, while the opposition 'Students' List' is projected to win at least 135 seats in the National Assembly.

item.title: New Air Defense Towers Built Around Putin's Valdai Residence, Exceeding 50 Total
item.description: An additional ring of 16 air defense towers has been constructed within a 50-kilometer radius of Vladimir Putin's Valdai residence. These new installations, likely housing Pantsir or Tor missile systems, expand the existing defense network, which includes a base near the residence and a facility on Lisiy Island.

item.title: New 265-Bed Oncology Center to Be Built in Tashkent with South Korean Support
item.description: Tashkent will construct a new 265-bed oncology center with the support of South Korea's AUM & LEE Architects & Associates. The Ministry of Health signed a contract for consulting services, which includes design, construction management, and equipment selection. The center will be part of a medical cluster funded by Korea Eximbank.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Urges Judges Not to Fear Security Service in Torture Case
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has called on judges to disregard fear of the State Committee for National Security (GKNB) when considering a case involving alleged torture. A woman accused GKNB investigators of fabricating charges and torturing her husband, who is detained on fraud suspicions. Japarov stressed the need for objective rulings.

item.title: Astana Bathhouse Complex Fire Forces Evacuation of 60 People
item.description: A fire broke out in the roof of a hotel and bathhouse complex in Astana, leading to the evacuation of 60 individuals. The Ministry of Emergency Situations reported that the fire, covering 10 square meters, was caused by the ignition of insulation and electrical cables in the ventilation system.

item.title: CENTCOM Reports Over 95 Percent of Ships Safely Transited Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that over 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil have been shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, with more than 95 percent of vessels passing safely. CENTCOM stated that its forces cleared all naval mines laid by Iran, ensuring safe passage for commercial vessels.

item.title: Kyrgyz Gold Miner Appeals to President for Review of Processing Volume Limits
item.description: A gold miner from Kyrgyzstan's Chatkal district has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov to reconsider restrictions on the volume of gold-bearing material processed. The entrepreneur cited short mining seasons due to climate and lengthy document processing as challenges.

item.title: Russia redirects grain exports south and east, impacting Central Asian markets
item.description: Central Asia's grain market is transforming as Russia redirects exports due to logistical constraints. Uzbekistan increases processing and challenges Kazakhstan's flour market share in Afghanistan, while Russia emerges as a significant supplier. Kazakhstan remains a key producer, but Russian wheat may challenge its dominance.

item.title: Remittance inflows to Kyrgyzstan reached $269.6 million in August
item.description: In August, remittance inflows to Kyrgyzstan amounted to $269.6 million, according to the National Bank. Outflows from Kyrgyzstan totaled $8.7 million during the same period. The majority of incoming funds, $240.9 million, originated from CIS countries, primarily Russia ($239.2 million). Non-CIS countries contributed $28.7 million, with the US accounting for $24.1 million.

item.title: Audi to Open First US Factory, Trump Announces $4 Billion Project
item.description: German automaker Audi is preparing to build its first factory in the United States. This move is partly influenced by import tariffs imposed by President Trump, which cost the company 1 billion euros last year. The project is valued at $4 billion.

item.title: Uzbekistan Bans Unapproved Meetings for School Directors
item.description: Uzbekistan's Deputy Prime Minister for Education, Erkinjon Turdimov, announced a ban on summoning school directors to meetings without prior ministry approval. He emphasized that school leaders should focus on their primary duties rather than attending numerous unscheduled gatherings. Turdimov stated that any required meeting must be approved by the ministry, and school principals should not be called to local government sessions.
